title: The Completely Optional Dessert
scene: You and a friend finish dinner feeling comfortably full. You both agree that dessert is unnecessary, then gradually turn sharing one dessert into a surprisingly delicate exercise in politeness.
sceneJa: 友人と夕食を食べ終え、二人とも十分お腹いっぱい。それでもデザートを1つだけシェアすることになり、最後のひとかけらを巡って妙に丁寧な譲り合いが始まる。

chunks.en: A friend and I went out for dinner
chunks.ja: 友人と二人で夕食を食べに行きました
小さなレストランへ

chunks.en: neither of us had tried before.
chunks.ja: どちらも行ったことのない
料理はとてもおいしかったのですが

chunks.en: but by the end of the main course,
chunks.ja: メインを食べ終えるころには
二人とも十分にお腹いっぱいでした

chunks.en: When the waiter brought the dessert menu,
chunks.ja: 店員がデザートメニューを持ってくると

chunks.en: my friend looked at me and said,
chunks.ja: 友人が私を見て言いました

chunks.en: We don’t need anything else, do we?
chunks.ja: 『もう何もいらないよな？』と
『絶対いらない』と私は答えました
メニューを開きながら
純粋に学術的な興味から
困ったことに

chunks.en: one of the desserts sounded unusually good,
chunks.ja: ひとつだけ妙においしそうなデザートがあり

chunks.en: so we agreed to order one
chunks.ja: 1個だけ頼むことにして
シェアすることにしました
デザートが届くと

chunks.en: my friend politely pushed the plate towards me
chunks.ja: 友人は丁寧に皿をこちらへ寄せ

chunks.en: and told me to have the first bite.
chunks.ja: 『最初に食べていいよ』と言いました
私は小さくひと口食べ
皿を戻し
確立できたように感じました
とても文明的な仕組みを
1分後には

chunks.en: we were both keeping a surprisingly close eye
chunks.ja: 二人とも驚くほど注意深く見ていました

chunks.en: on how much the other person
chunks.ja: 相手がどれくらい
一口ごとにスプーンへ取っているかを
どちらも何も言いませんでしたが

chunks.en: but the portions became gradually smaller
chunks.ja: 一口の量はだんだん小さくなり
デザートが減っていくにつれて
やがて
最後のひとかけらだけが残り

chunks.en: in the middle of the plate,
chunks.ja: 皿の中央に

chunks.en: surrounded by an impressive amount of diplomacy.
chunks.ja: その周囲には見事なほどの外交努力が漂っていました

chunks.en: My friend told me I could have it,
chunks.ja: 友人が『食べていいよ』と言ったので
当然私は断りました
結局それを残したまま
会計を済ませました
どうやら
おいしいデザートを無駄にする方が
〜が判明するよりはマシだったようです

chunks.en: which of us was less polite.
chunks.ja: どちらの方が礼儀知らずなのか

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: we were both keeping a surprisingly close eye / on how much the other person / was putting on each spoon
we were both / keeping a surprisingly / close eye on how much / the other person was putting
we were / both keeping a surprisingly close / eye on how much the other person was
questions.explanation: ‘Keep a close eye on ...’ works as one phrase, followed by the thing being watched and then the action being observed.

questions.question: What does ‘purely out of academic interest’ imply here?
options: The speaker genuinely needs to study the menu for research
The speaker jokingly pretends curiosity is the only reason for opening the dessert menu
The speaker is checking whether the menu contains academic vocabulary
questions.explanation: The phrase is deliberately over-formal. The speaker is really tempted by dessert and uses ‘academic interest’ as a dry excuse.

questions.question: Why do they leave the final piece uneaten?
options: Neither of them likes the dessert anymore
They are both too polite to take the last piece after offering it to the other person
The waiter asks them not to finish it
questions.explanation: The humour comes from politeness becoming so strong that wasting the dessert feels easier than revealing who wants the last bite more.

speak: Start relaxed and satisfied. Let the curiosity creep in at ‘purely out of academic interest.’ Keep the middle section calm and observant rather than competitive. Pause slightly before the final sentence and deliver ‘was preferable to discovering which of us was less polite’ with quiet, matter-of-fact seriousness.
review: Today’s flow: comfortably full → unnecessary menu → one small exception → polite sharing → silent competition → diplomatic stalemate. Useful chunks: ‘purely out of ...’ for motives, ‘keep a close eye on ...’ for careful attention, and ‘be preferable to ...’ for calmly comparing two imperfect options.
